transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I'm convening our pre-filing case conference today. As you all know, our former sales executive departed last week to join a direct competitor, and we believe confidential customer information may have been used after that departure. We're looking at a potential preliminary-injunction hearing within three weeks. Before I can sign off on our filing decision, I need to hear from each of you. Employment counsel, forensics counsel, and insurance counsel — please report any material issues on your end regarding the draft filing, which currently seeks broad relief covering customer information, pricing materials, and source-code documentation. I'll record authorization subject to any prerequisites that must be completed before we file.

transcript.text: Director, I need to report a material issue. While checking the former executive's archived personnel file, I found a signed separation agreement containing an exclusive forum clause requiring disputes about confidential information to be filed in Illinois state court in Cook County, where the executive worked. I have not yet added this clause to the draft strategy memorandum. This could affect where we file and may be a prerequisite to resolve before filing.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Director, I need to report a material issue from my forensic review. I reviewed the access logs and forensic image this week, and I confirmed that the only company data copied to the executive's device was the customer-list database. The review did not show any copying of pricing materials or source-code documentation. I have not yet updated the evidence chart to reflect these findings. This is relevant because our draft filing currently seeks broad relief covering all three categories of information, and we may be overreaching on pricing materials and source-code documentation based on what the forensic evidence actually supports.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Director, I need to report a material issue from the insurance side. I confirmed with our broker this week that our applicable cyber-and-crime endorsement requires the carrier's written consent before the company seeks injunctive relief against an employee. This confirmation is still outside the litigation file and needs to be addressed before we file, since filing without the carrier's written consent could jeopardize our coverage position.
